content.text: In scripts/run-pipeline.ts only (plus its tests if any): the dry run searched 1 company, not 10, because the default ICP (industry "Software") filters out most fixtures. Use an open ICP for the runner (no industry, size, location or keyword filters), the same open ICP that tests/agent/baseline-run.test.ts uses for its open ICP run, and put the ICP description text in one constant at the top of the script. Also: when --llm fake is used, label token counts as simulated, not measured, and keep measured only for real gateway usage. Then run npx vitest run, npx tsc --noEmit and npm run lint. Do not run the script. Summarise in 3 bullets.

content.text:
- **ICP:** `scripts/run-pipeline.ts` now uses the open ICP from `tests/agent/helpers.ts`: `industry: ""` and no size, location, keyword or excluded-domain filters. The description text, "Companies in any industry of any size in any location.", is one constant at the top. I hardcoded it to match `describeIcp(OPEN_ICP)` instead of calling `describeIcp`, so it won't follow if that function changes. It's printed in the console output and added to the JSON report as `icp_description`.
- **Tokens:** the console line now reads `(simulated)` with `--llm fake` and `(measured)` with `--llm real`. The report's `llm` block has a new `token_basis` field with the same value.
- **Checks:** `npx vitest run` passed (153 tests in 10 files), and `tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` finished with no errors. I didn't run the script, so I haven't confirmed the dry run now searches 10 companies. I added no tests, since the script has none.
